cards.text: Joash spent six years hidden in the house of God, until Jehoiada the priest crowned him king (2 Chronicles 22:12, 23:11). Joash is seven years old when he becomes king of Judah, and he reigns in Jerusalem forty years. His mother is Zibiah, from Beersheba.

cards.question: Young King Joash does what is right in the eyes of the LORD. How long does that last?

answers.text: All the days of Jehoiada the priest
All forty years of his reign
Only for his first seven years

cards.text: Jehoiada takes two wives for Joash, and sons and daughters follow. Some time later, the king who grew up hidden in the house of God sets his heart on a big project.

cards.question: What project does King Joash set his heart on?

answers.text: Repairing the house of the LORD

cards.text: So Joash gathers the priests and Levites: go out to the cities of Judah and collect the money due every year from all Israel, to repair the house of your God. Then the king adds, "Do it quickly."

cards.question: King Joash tells the Levites to collect the money quickly. Soon he has to call in Jehoiada the high priest about it. True or false: The Levites hurry right out to collect the money.

cards.text: The Levites do NOT make haste, and friend, I know slow: I spent years in a junk drawer watching dust land. So King Joash calls in Jehoiada the high priest.

cards.question: King Joash asks Jehoiada why the Levites haven't brought in the tax for the Tent of the Testimony. True or false: The king says that tax was imposed by Moses and the assembly of Israel.

cards.text: Some background, friend: before Joash, Athaliah ruled the land, and later the people tore down the temple of Baal (2 Chronicles 22:12, 23:17). Here the text calls her that wicked woman Athaliah.

cards.question: The text explains what the sons of Athaliah had done to the house of God. What was it?

answers.text: They broke in and used its sacred objects for the Baals
They tore down its walls and burned its wooden doors
They stripped its gold and carried it off to Egypt

cards.text: So at King Joash's command, a chest is made, a place for the people to bring in that tax.

cards.question: King Joash's chest is placed outside, at the ___ of the house of the LORD.

cards.text: Then a proclamation goes out across Judah and Jerusalem: bring to the LORD the tax Moses the servant of God set on Israel in the wilderness. Same tax, brand new chest.

cards.question: When the proclamation goes out, all the officers and all the people ___ and drop their contributions in the chest until it's full.

cards.text: Whenever the Levites bring the chest to the king's overseers and there's a large amount of money, the royal scribe and the high priest's officer empty it. Then they carry it back to its place.

cards.question: The royal scribe and the high priest's officer empty the chest every ___.

cards.text: They gather money in ABUNDANCE, friend. I've watched a cookie jar go from full to empty that fast, but NEVER from empty to full.

cards.question: True or false: King Joash and Jehoiada give the money to the men supervising the work on the house of the LORD.
The supervisors use the money to hire workers to restore the house of the LORD. Who do they hire?

cards.text: So the workmen labor, and the repair work moves along in their hands.

cards.question: True or false: The workmen rebuild the house of God in a brand new design.

cards.text: They restore the house of God to its specifications, and they reinforce it. And when they finish, there's money LEFT OVER, and friend, I have NEVER in my life seen a repair job come in under budget.

cards.question: What happens to the money left over from repairing the house of the LORD?

answers.text: It's used to make articles for the house of the LORD
It's stored away in the king's treasury
It's handed back to the people of Judah

cards.text: Utensils for the service and the burnt offerings, dishes, and other objects of gold and silver, all made for the house of the LORD.

cards.question: Throughout the days of Jehoiada, burnt offerings are presented ___ in the house of the LORD.

cards.text: I think this part is heavy, friend. Jehoiada the priest is old and full of years, and he dies.

cards.question: Jehoiada the priest dies at the age of ___.

cards.text: They bury Jehoiada with the kings, in the City of David.

cards.question: Why is Jehoiada the priest buried with the kings?

answers.text: He did what was good in Israel for God and His temple
He ruled Judah as king while Joash was young
He led Judah's army to a great victory in battle

cards.text: And Joash? He's still on that throne, friend, and his story isn't over yet.
